A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Embodied-R1 and retain matching core methods, datasets, and experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original spatial and pointing evaluations, SIMPLEREnv and real-world robot experiments, and training and reward ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds LIBERO policy evaluations, complex real-world demonstrations, execution-time comparisons, and updated RGB-D results.

M1.justification: The core pointing model and RFT curriculum remain, but v2 implements extensions that v1 left as future work: visual-trace-conditioned Diffusion Policy, periodic replanning, Gemini-based task decomposition, and contact-sensitive controllers. Appendix F also presents a dual-encoder RGB-D architecture with RefSpatial alignment through SFT before 3D RFT, extending the earlier RGB-D fine-tuning account.

E1.justification: LIBERO expands from qualitative trace examples in v1 to executed policy evaluations across 40 Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long tasks in v2 Appendix F. v2 also uses RefSpatial alignment data and adds real-world sorting, multistep organization, mathematically grounded placement, wiping, and bottle pressing. Open6DOR coverage is retained in the appendix.

E2.justification: The SIMPLEREnv comparison replaces RT-1-X, RoboVLM, and SpatialVLA entries with π0, π0-fast, OpenVLA-OFT, ThinkAct, and Magma. v2 also adds MOKA to the eight-task real-world comparison, evaluates A0 trajectories, introduces a Diffusion Policy baseline, and includes OpenVLA (FT) in execution-time comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include 50 demonstrations per LIBERO task, trace updates every 15 steps on LIBERO-Long, and a bottle-pressing policy trained on 50 demonstrations. SIMPLEREnv reporting changes to 24 episodes per task, removes the grasp-success metric, and changes baseline-result provenance. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds complex-task case studies in Figure 8, A0 trajectory comparisons in Figure 10, and execution-time and failure analyses in Appendix D. Table 12 tests the benefit of trace conditioning for Diffusion Policy. Existing common-sense, SFT/RFT reasoning, mixed-training, and trajectory-point-count ablations remain substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 Table 5 explicitly averages Embodied-R1 and SoFar results over three rounds of 24 runs. v2 Table 4 states 24 episodes per task but omits the three-round aggregation information. This changes statistical reporting without establishing an actual reduction in runs. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or variability estimates for these results.

E6.justification: New results include LIBERO averages of 64.4% for Diffusion Policy and 79.4% with Embodied-R1, MOKA's 9.2% real-world average, and execution-time measurements. RGB-D Level0/Level1/overall scores change from 99.8/50.9/90.2 to 99.2/74.5/94.3 under the revised model and training account. SIMPLEREnv baseline scores are replaced, including OpenVLA's 1.0% versus 5.2% average, and grasp results are removed. The headline 56.2% and 87.5% results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Equations 1–2 explicitly define the normalized GRPO advantage and clipped objective; v2 replaces these equations with a verbal summary. This reduces formal mathematical specification without establishing a changed optimization rule. The pointing definitions and principal reward equations remain, and neither version develops theorem or proof results.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified embodiment-agnostic pointing, four capabilities, Embodied-Points-200K, a 3B model trained through RFT, and strong zero-shot manipulation. The headline benchmark coverage and success rates are unchanged; revised wording emphasizes ideas already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking policy improvements to dense trajectory constraints and execution efficiency to single-pass inference, alongside MOKA failure mechanisms. Learned-policy integration changes from untested future work to preliminary demonstrated capability, and physical common-sense hallucinations become an explicit limitation. The RGB-D discussion becomes more positive, although Appendix G retains an earlier deficit description inconsistent with the updated Table 13.

D1.justification: v2 identifies EasyR1 and CleanDiffuser, provides specific model and dataset links, and documents new alignment stages, planner/controller choices, demonstration counts, and replanning intervals. Core hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Conversely, v2 removes details explaining construction of the SFT/RL reasoning ablation and the six-trial count for visual-disturbance testing.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial discussion of VLM reasoning through RFT, including Seg-Zero, VisionReasoner, and Reason-RFT. Appendix H and Table 14 systematically position Embodied-R1 against RoboPoint, RoboBrain, A0, and FSD across representations, capabilities, and reasoning. Additional policy-learning and RGB-D references, alongside removed older citations, materially revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, architecture description, training explanation, and experimental discussion undergo extensive condensation and rewriting. Related Work moves before the method, analysis and ablations are merged, and RGB-D evaluation moves into the appendix. The appendices are reorganized and expanded, with additional authorship, funding, and LLM-use disclosures.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is rearranged into a compact four-panel display, and existing generalization examples are incorporated into the composite Figure 5. v2 adds complex-task and A0 comparison figures and tables for latency, LIBERO, and method positioning. The SIMPLEREnv table is redesigned without grasp columns, while the Open6DOR table moves to the appendix. Typography and captions also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for pointing as a general manipulation interface: v1 left learned-policy integration untested, whereas v2 evaluates it across 40 LIBERO tasks and demonstrates long-horizon and contact-rich execution. The RGB-D design and expanded comparisons further improve assessability. These gains outweigh reporting regressions: Table 4's π0-fast scores average 32.1%, not the stated 48.3%; repeated-round information is lost; and Appendix G retains an RGB-D limitation contradicted by Table 13.
